variant_title_en: Time — Reading Time and Adding/Subtracting Time
story_theme_en: Lin planned her Monday morning schedule. She wakes up at 07:30. Bathing and getting dressed takes 45 minutes. Eating breakfast takes 25 minutes and walking to school takes 20 minutes. Lin needs to leave at what time to arrive at school on time at 08:30?
helper_tip_en: Have students draw the clock face and move the hands step by step to find each new time.
think_story_en: Wake at 07:30 + 45 min bathing = 08:15. + 25 min breakfast = 08:40. + 20 min walking = 09:00. Lin must leave at 08:40 to arrive at school by 08:30 on time.

data.question: Lin started her homework at 14:45 and finished at 16:10. How long did she study?
data.explanation: 14:45 to 15:00 = 15 min, 15:00 to 16:00 = 1 hour, 16:00 to 16:10 = 10 min. Total = 1 hour 25 minutes

explanation_steps_en: Time uses two systems: 12-hour (AM/PM) and 24-hour format.
1 hour = 60 minutes. Half an hour = 30 minutes. A quarter hour = 15 minutes.
When adding time, add the minutes first. If the total exceeds 60, convert to hours.
When subtracting time, if the minutes being subtracted are more than the available minutes, borrow 1 hour = 60 minutes.
Finding elapsed time: End Time − Start Time = Duration.
A timeline or number line can help visualize the time passing.

worked_examples_en.question_en: Ai started reading at 09:15 and read for 1 hour 40 minutes. What time did Ai finish?

common_mistakes_en: Forgetting that 1 hour = 60 minutes and not converting when minutes exceed 60.
Confusing AM (before noon) with PM (after noon).
Subtracting time directly without borrowing 1 hour (= 60 min) when the minutes to subtract are larger.
hints_en: Use a timeline or number line to visualize the time passing.
Check your answer by working backward.

explanation_en: Time is measured in hours and minutes. 1 hour = 60 minutes. To add time, add minutes first and convert if minutes exceed 60. To subtract time, borrow 1 hour (60 min) when needed. Elapsed time = end time − start time.
